summary: Selects the most recently changed matching channels from multiple CHOP inputs, using the first input as the default output channel set.
key_concepts: Override CHOP outputs the most recently changed matching values from several inputs.
The first input defines the output channel names and length, and later inputs only override matching channels.
Match can compare channels by index or by name; name matching is safer when channel order may change.
If multiple inputs change the same matched channel at the same time, later input order determines which value wins.
Changing the number of inputs or the match mode resets output to the first input's default values.
Make Index adds a channel showing which input most recently supplied each overridden value.

key_params.name: match
key_params.note: Match monitored channels by channel number or channel name

key_params.name: makeindex
key_params.note: Create an output index channel identifying which input last changed

key_params.name: indexname

common_gotchas: Override CHOP is active; DocsBrain can misclassify it as deprecated because only the Monitor on Input Cooks parameter is deprecated.
The output channels and length are based on the first input; extra or missing channels on later inputs are ignored.
Changing the input count or match mode resets the output to the first input's default values.
When two inputs change the same matched channel at the same time, input order decides precedence.
Matching by number is brittle when input channel order changes; matching by name is safer for device/preset handoff rigs.
Use the optional index channel when downstream logic needs to know which source last won control.
build_relevance: 2021.10000+ multi-source CHOP override and last-change control routing
